## Design

### 2026-10-09 – I was trying to make a discrete calculator with a dial, so i started brainstorming. i started to throw ideas at the wall, seeing what'd stick, and i was stuck on output method. there are so many ways:

**5h**

I was trying to make a discrete calculator with a dial, so i started brainstorming. i started to throw ideas at the wall, seeing what'd stick, and i was stuck on output method. there are so many ways: screen, pneumatics yes a guy made a clock on [youtube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E1BLGpE5zH0), but i landed on vibration. i then realized the insane ass potential for a discrete, small, and blind-friendly calculator, so i scrapped any visual ideas i had and got to work in kicad. i forgot to log a bunch of entries so this is my manifesto? i think. so anyways, i wanted to use an STM32 because god im so used to them and even if STMicroelectronics are bitches they make some reeeeeeeeeaaaaaaaally good MCU's. i landed on an STM32C031, ARM Cortex-M0+, and for the dial i ended up on a rotary encoder with a switch. here's all the photos!
